## 1. Data integrity

- The verified snapshot and the `get_indicators` outputs agree at the snapshot's rounding for every shared indicator: 10 EMA 131.08, 50 SMA 167.81, 200 SMA 173.31, RSI 27.44, MACD -13.56, lower Bollinger band 110.66, ATR 9.46. I found no discrepancies.
- VWMA (137.30) appears only in the `get_indicators` output, not in the snapshot. I report it as tool output, not as a snapshot-verified figure.
- The 2026-11-17 volume of 9,082,209 is not rounded to the nearest hundred like nearly every other row in the series. It may be a still-forming or provisional bar. Treat today's close (115.02), volume and range as potentially subject to revision. This is an inference from the number's format, not something a tool confirmed.

## 2. Indicators selected (8) and why

| Role | Indicator | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Short-term trend | close_10_ema | Fast read on momentum and on where bounces might stall |
| Medium-term trend | close_50_sma | Dynamic resistance and trend direction |
| Long-term trend | close_200_sma | Strategic regime, and the 50/200 relationship |
| Momentum/trend | macd (macds and macdh read from the snapshot) | Confirms whether the downtrend is accelerating or fading |
| Momentum extremes | rsi | Oversold flag and divergence check |
| Volatility/extremes | boll_lb (boll and boll_ub from the snapshot) | Statistical stretch and band geometry |
| Risk | atr | Stop distance and position sizing |
| Volume-weighted trend | vwma | Where the volume-weighted cost basis sits relative to price |

The set is complementary: three trend horizons, one momentum oscillator, one trend-momentum indicator, one volatility envelope, one risk measure and one volume-weighted measure. I left out the upper Bollinger band, the signal line and the histogram as separate pulls to avoid redundancy. The snapshot supplies their latest values anyway.

## 3. Verified price action

**Latest bar (2026-11-17):** open 117.73, high 121.61, low 114.12, close 115.02, volume 9,082,209. The close sits in the lower part of the day's range.

**Context from the fetched window (2026-05-18 to 2026-11-17):**
- The latest close of 115.02 and the intraday low of 114.12 are the lowest in the entire fetched window. The prior lowest close was 127.65 on 2026-11-13, and the prior lowest intraday low was 117.32 on 2026-11-16. Within this window there is no earlier price history below the current level, so I have no tool-supported support level to cite below 114.12.
- The recent peak close was 201.05 on 2026-09-21. From there to 115.02 is about -42.8% on a close-to-close basis, over roughly eight weeks.
- A sharp leg lower began on 2026-10-30. The close fell from 160.59 (10/29) to 143.54 on volume of 20,894,000, the heaviest of that stretch, about -10.6% in one session.
- The rebound after that was brief. The close reached 151.50 on 11/04, then fell back to 136.82 on 11/05, and the series has made lower closes since 11/11: 136.27 → 130.67 → 127.65 → 119.84 → 115.02.
- Gap-downs on the last two sessions: the 11/16 open was 119.31 against a prior close of 127.65, and the 11/17 open was 117.73 against a prior close of 119.84. Sellers have not been bought into at the open.
- The 11/16 session carried 11,226,100 shares, above most of the sessions around it, so the latest leg down has had participation.

## 4. Trend structure (moving averages)

| Level | Value | Close vs. level |
|---|---|---|
| 10 EMA | 131.08 | Close is 16.06 below |
| 50 SMA | 167.81 | Close is 52.79 below |
| 200 SMA | 173.31 | Close is 58.29 below |
| Bollinger middle (20 SMA) | 145.09 | Close is 30.07 below |

- **Alignment is bearish at every horizon:** price < 10 EMA < VWMA < Bollinger mid < 50 SMA < 200 SMA.
- **The 50 SMA is below the 200 SMA** (167.81 vs 173.31). Across the entire 30-day lookback the 50 SMA stayed under the 200 SMA (for example 177.93 vs 182.03 on 10/19). I can't date the crossover from this output, so I don't claim when it happened.
- **Both long averages are falling.** The 50 SMA slid from 180.32 on 10/29 to 167.81. The 200 SMA slid from 182.03 on 10/19 to 173.31. Neither has turned up.
- **The 10 EMA has fallen on every trading day in the window** (177.70 on 10/19 to 131.08). This is a persistent down-slope, not a pause.
- **Reference points for a bounce.** These are derived from the latest tool values and recent prices, not historically validated:
  - The nearest overhead markers are the 11/16 high of 122.99 and the 11/17 high of 121.61.
  - Above those sit the 11/13 close of 127.65 and the 10 EMA at 131.08.
  - Beyond that are the VWMA (137.30) and the Bollinger middle band (145.09).

## 5. Momentum: MACD and RSI

**MACD**
- MACD is -13.56, the signal line is -11.42 and the histogram is -2.14. MACD is below its signal, and both are well below zero.
- MACD has gotten more negative nearly every session since 10/19 (-1.91), reaching -12.75 on 11/16 and -13.56 now. There is no bullish crossover and no sign yet of momentum turning up.
- The negative histogram says downside momentum is still expanding, not exhausting.

**RSI**
- RSI is 27.44, below the conventional 30 oversold threshold. It was 29.23 on 11/16 and 32.43 on 11/13.
- It has stayed in a depressed band since 10/30 (readings from 29.70 to 40.65). The 40.65 reading on 11/04 marks the high of the failed bounce.
- **No bullish divergence is visible.** On 11/02 the close was 137.83 with RSI at 29.70. On 11/17 the close is 115.02 and RSI is lower at 27.44, so the new price low is confirmed by momentum.
- In strong downtrends RSI can stay below 30 for extended periods, so an oversold reading alone is not a reversal signal. Look for RSI to hold above its recent lows while price makes a lower low, or to reclaim 30.

## 6. Volatility and volume

**Bollinger Bands**
- The bands are lower 110.66, middle 145.09 and upper 179.52, so the width is about 68.86.
- The close at 115.02 is 4.36 above the lower band, and the intraday low of 114.12 was also above it. Price is hugging the lower band without a confirmed close below it.
- The lower band itself has fallen steadily, from 166.12 on 10/19 to 110.66 now, and the upper band is far above at 179.52. Price pressing the band while the band slopes down is the "riding the band" behavior the indicator warns about. A touch of the band is not by itself a buy signal.
- A close below 110.66 would show the downtrend extending beyond a two-standard-deviation stretch.

**ATR**
- ATR is 9.46, about 8.2% of the latest close. It peaked in this window at 11.06 on 11/05 and has eased since, even as price kept falling. The decline is mostly orderly selling rather than a panic expansion, though the 10/30 and 11/05 sessions were large.
- Illustrative stop distances from the current close, arithmetic only: 1.5 × ATR is about 14.2 points, which puts a long stop around 100.8, and 2 × ATR is about 18.9 points, which puts one around 96.1. A short position's equivalent distances would be above the entry price. With daily ranges this wide, position sizing matters more than stop placement.

**VWMA**
- VWMA is 137.30, above the close by 22.28. Volume-weighted prices over the lookback sit well above the current price, and the heavy-volume days (10/30 at 143.54, 11/05 at 136.82) closed above today's level. That implies much of the recent traded volume is now at a loss, which can act as supply on rallies. This is an interpretation, not something the tools verified.
- VWMA has fallen every day in the window (180.87 on 10/19 to 137.30), consistent with the other trend measures.

## 7. Scenarios (for the deciding agent, not a recommendation)

**Bearish continuation (currently favored by every trend and momentum measure):**
- Price is below all moving averages and the VWMA, and the MACD and RSI lows are being confirmed.
- A close below the lower band (110.66) would be a further confirmation.
- The risk to this view is the mean-reversion pressure that comes with RSI under 30 and price hugging the band.

**Relief bounce (possible, low-confirmation):**
- Oversold RSI and a stretched distance from the 10 EMA (16.06 points) make a sharp countertrend rally plausible.
- The prior bounce reached the 11/04 close of 151.50 before failing, and that move began after a high-volume low.
- Reasonable first hurdles are 121.61-122.99, then 127.65 and 131.08. A bounce that cannot reclaim the 10 EMA would remain consistent with the downtrend.

**Evidence that would change the picture:**
- RSI holding above its recent lows while price prints a lower low.
- MACD histogram shrinking toward zero.
- A close back above the 10 EMA (131.08) on rising volume.
- A reversal candle on a full-session volume figure (today's volume may be incomplete).

  - Retail capitulation, with losses on calls.
  - Persistent underperformance relative to BTC.
- Potential upside catalysts:
  - Mean reversion or a short squeeze, since some posters hint at heavily short positioning.
  - BTC strength eventually carrying over to COIN.
  - Institutional-adoption narratives.
- No earnings dates, regulatory headlines or other event catalysts appear in the data. The news feed was unavailable, so any such events are unknown to me.
- Heavy capitulation language can be a contrarian signal, but this sample is too small and one-day to rely on that.

**5. Summary table**

| User-tagged ratio | Slightly bearish, very low sample | StockTwits | 2 Bullish (9%) vs 3 Bearish (14%), 17 unlabeled |

With news and Reddit missing, the sample small and one-day, and mostly unlabeled posts, this is weak evidence. It should be weighed alongside fundamentals and technicals and is not a price call.

# COIN (Coinbase Global, Inc.) Fundamental Report, as of 2026-11-17

**Scope and data caveats**
- Sources are the five fundamentals and insider tools. Financial statements come from SEC EDGAR filings made on or before 2026-11-17, so the latest period is the quarter ended 2026-09-30 (Q3 2026).
- None of these tools returns a news feed or a price series. "Past week" therefore means the most recent filings and data, not a weekly event log.
- Quarterly income-statement columns omit Q4 because Q4 sits in the 10-K. Cash-flow figures are cumulative year-to-date, so I derived the standalone quarters.
- Items marked *(derived)* are my own arithmetic and were not reported by a tool.

---

| Metric | Value |

| Company / sector | Coinbase Global, Inc. / Financial Services, Financial Data & Stock Exchanges (NMS) |
| Market cap | ~$30.45B |
| Implied share price *(derived)* | ~$115. Both P/B 2.18 × book value $52.65 and forward EPS $2.455 × forward P/E 46.85 give ~$115. |

**Takeaways**
- The implied price of ~$115 sits within about 1% of the 52-week low. It is about 60% below the 52-week high, about 32% below the 50-day average and about 34% below the 200-day average.
- The insider tape shows sales at $186–$198 on 2026-10-02. If the implied price is right, the stock has fallen roughly 40% in about six weeks. A price-data agent should confirm this, because I could not verify price directly.
- A beta of 3.35 means very large swings relative to the market, so position sizing matters.
- The forward P/E of ~47x on a low earnings base is not cheap on earnings. P/B of 2.2x and P/S of 5.6x are modest by this stock's own history.

---

## 2. Income statement trends (quarterly, USD millions)

| Quarter | Revenue | Operating income | Op. margin *(derived)* | Net income | Diluted EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 2025 | 2,034 | 706 | 34.7% | 66 | 0.24 |
| Q2 2025 | 1,497 | –25 | –1.7% | 1,429 | 5.14 |
| Q3 2025 | 1,869 | 481 | 25.7% | 433 | 1.50 |
| Q1 2026 | 1,413 | –21 | –1.5% | –394 | –1.49 |
| Q2 2026 | 1,220 | –113 | –9.3% | –359 | –1.36 |
| **Q3 2026** | **1,216** | **62** | **5.1%** | **719** | **2.51** |

**Findings**
1. **Revenue is shrinking.** Q3 2026 revenue of $1,216M is down about 35% year over year. Q2 was down about 18.5% and Q1 about 30.5%. Nine-month 2026 revenue of $3,849M is about 29% below the same period of 2025 ($5,400M). Revenue has now been flat at roughly $1.2B for two quarters (1,220 then 1,216), which may suggest stabilization at a lower level.
2. **Core profitability is thin.** Operating income was negative in two of the three 2026 quarters. Q3 swung to +$62M, a 5.1% margin. TTM operating margin is 0.12%, against 25–35% in strong 2025 quarters. That suggests high operating leverage to trading volume.
3. **GAAP net income is a poor guide to operating performance.** Q3 2026 net income of $719M is more than 11 times operating income of $62M. Q2 2025 was similar, with a $1,429M profit on a –$25M operating loss. The gap implies large non-operating items. The most likely driver is mark-to-market on crypto holdings, but these tools do not break it out, so check the 10-Q. The Q3 EPS of $2.51 should not be treated as run-rate earnings.
4. **TTM figures.** Revenue is $5.44B and net income is –$702M (–12.9% margin). Comparing these with the Q1–Q3 2026 sums implies Q4 2025 revenue of ~$1.59B and a net loss of ~$668M *(derived)*. EBITDA is $271.5M, ROE is –4.7%, and the vendor reports gross profit of $4.64B (~85% of revenue). The statement itself leaves cost of revenue and gross profit untagged, so treat the vendor gross margin with care.

---

## 3. Balance sheet (USD millions)

| 2025-09-30 | 31,351 | 11,990 | 15,328 | 16,023 |
| 2025-12-31 | 29,672 | 11,285 | 14,879 | 14,793 |
| 2026-03-31 | 28,849 | 10,205 | 15,368 | 13,481 |
| 2026-06-30 | 26,460 | 8,614 | 13,381 | 13,080 |
| 2026-09-30 | 27,385 | 8,604 | 13,445 | 13,940 |

**Findings**
- **Liquidity is sound.** The current ratio is 2.43 (current assets $17.6B vs current liabilities $7.3B, consistent with the reported figure). Cash is $8.6B, about 28% of market cap.
